newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones dropped 86.58 points to 6,746.90. PLDT's ADR inched up $0 3/4 to $59 5/8.
* The peso closed weaker at 26.34 to a U.S. dollar from 26.331.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index dipped 2.85 points to 3,396.04.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 10.5625 percent.

*Keener competition and abundant food supply in local markets contained Philippine inflation to an annualised 5.0 percent in January, down from 5.2 percent in December last year, economists said on Wednesday. The month-on-month inflation rate slowed down to 0.6 percent in January from 0.8 percent the previous month, the National Statistics Office (NSO) said.

* Jollibee Foods Corp said on Wednesday it plans to raise funds of at least 1.5 billion pesos in domestic capital markets in this quarter. Raffy de la Rosa, the company's chief finance officer, said during an analysts' briefing the company is looking at issuing new shares or warrants, or offering a convertible bond.

* The Philippine's National Telecommunication Commission (NTC) has approved the application of Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc (Digitel) to implement new rates. Under an NTC order announced on Wednesday, Digitel subscribers will be allowed to choose payment programmes with monthly fees as low as 150 pesos a month to as high as 750 pesos a month.

* Ultrana Energy and Resources Corp said on Wednesday CMS Generationa Pinamucan Ltd Duration Co, an affiliate of U.S.-based CMS Energy Corp, had acquired a 29.46 percent stake in Ultrana's Magellan Cogeneration Inc. President Roberto Cokeng told the Philippine Stock Exchange that CMS had also entered into a shareholders agreement whereby CMS would later raise its interest to 44 percent.
*Republic Glass Holdings Corp said on Wednesday it made a net income of 309.262 million pesos in 1996 compared with 308.238 million in the previous year.
*Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co posted 1996 net income of 6.44 billion pesos, up 11.98 percent from 5.751 billion pesos the previous year.
*Magnum Holdings Inc said on Wednesday it posted a net loss of 2.38 million pesos in 1996 on total income of 4.19 million pesos.

*Property developer and chemicals manufacturer A.Brown Company Inc said on Wednesday it posted a net income of 205.237 million pesos for 1996. The results announcement did not give a comparative year-ago figure. But A.Brown had earlier reported a net income of 214.3 million pesos in 1995.
*Philippine Commercial International Bank (PCIBank) said on Wednesday its net income in the fourth quarter ended December 31, 1996 amounted to 681.262 million pesos.
